nina: rolling prod canary for INT8 kernel-selection + jittered-batching now (09:30 PT). canary 5% -> 30% -> 100% if green.

deploy-bot: deploy started: commit 9c4b1a0 -> prod | canary=5% -> 30% -> 100% | sha 9c4b1a0 | eta 00:22:00

kevin: pulled 45m of metrics at 100%: headline wins: p50 -15%, p95 -40%, p99 -33%, cost per 1k tokens -35%. numbers below.

kevin: ```
baseline: {p50: 120ms, p95: 310ms, p99: 720ms, cost_1k: $0.060}
after:    {p50: 102ms, p95: 186ms, p99: 482ms, cost_1k: $0.039}
```

lee: thanks — how broadly does INT8 apply? any model-size exclusions?

nina: INT8 enabled for medium+ transformer families (up to 30B tested). tiny models already quantized; huge 70B+ are on opt-in only due to quality checks. kernel selector prefers INT8 when seq_len <= 1024 and perf model mismatch is low.

kevin: jittered-batching aggregated small concurrent requests into variable windows (2-12ms based on current qps) to avoid synchronized bursts; reduced tail amplification.

runtime-oncall: infra looked stable. saw ephemeral queue bump during 30% step (~75s) but no OOMs. one routed fallback to FP16 for a 70B family because checksum mismatch detected; fallback worked.

infra: please add a metric for kernel_mismatch_rate to the runtime dashboard so we can monitor fallback frequency.

nina: added dashboard tile and PR #4520 for alert (kernel_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 10m).

product: can we get a short customer note? they'd like simple bullets and links to known caveats.

nina: draft blurb: "Many customers will see ~25-35% lower inference unit costs and faster p95 for common short/medium contexts. Large-context or opt-in large models may see smaller savings; quality is unchanged for tested models. Contact support for model-specific guidance."

kevin: posting internal perf graphs: https://internal.redwood/perf/graphs/1792509876 (internal-only).

deploy-bot: deploy finished: commit 9c4b1a0 -> prod | status=success | duration=00:27:45 :rocket:

runtime-oncall: monitoring for 72h. will revert if p99 regresses beyond baseline or kernel_mismatch_rate spikes. thumbs up to the infra and quant team! :tada:
